title: Dedicated pool throttle accounting and SLA mediation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a robust accounting system for transient throttles and tenant-level SLA mediation when dedicated GPU pools enter congestion. Current metering captures aggregate reserved throughput vs usage but lacks a reliable way to: (1) attribute short-duration throttles to tenants, (2) compute prorated SLA credits when bursts are denied or rate-limited, and (3) reconcile retrospective adjustments without double-counting.

Background and motivators:
- Customers with Dedicated pools buy reserved throughput and expect predictable latency/throughput. When pools become congested (hardware issues, noisy neighbors, autoscaler lag), we temporarily throttle or reject requests per-pool policy.
- Throttles today are surfaced as 429s and an uptime metric, but customers frequently ask for precise financial credit calculations and per-tenant explanations.
- Existing billing artifacts (reserved units ledger, burst credits) were designed for steady-state deficits; they do not capture fine-grained temporal attribution necessary for correct SLA crediting or to support tiered priority mediation.

Goals and non-goals:
Goals:
- Produce a deterministic ledger model that records: per-tenant reserved consumption, burst usage, throttle windows (start/end), and the system reason (capacity, region-failover, maintenance).
- Compute SLA credits that are: time-proportional, priority-aware (tenant-tier weighting), and resistant to replay/double-apply when retroactive reconciliations occur.
- Provide APIs and console views for customers to inspect throttle episodes, affected requests, and resulting credit calculations.
- Support automated roll-forward adjustments (post-incident reconciliation) with audit trails.
Non-goals:
- Rework global pricing or reserved contract terms. This ticket focuses on accounting and tooling only.

Proposed approach (high-level):
1) Event-first ledger: introduce a write-once event stream for pool-level episodes and tenant-attributed throttle events. Each event records: pool_id, epoch_ms (start/end), event_type (throttle_start/throttle_end/partial_degrade), affected_tenants (with weights), capacity_snapshot (reserved, available), and a monotonic sequence id.
2) Tenant micro-ledgers: derive per-tenant consumption slices from events combined with tokenized reserved-usage records. Micro-ledgers store time-windowed debits/credits keyed by day and sub-second token bucket windows (we will use 1s granularity for initial implementation).
3) Priority-aware mediation: when throttle occurs, apply a priority mediation policy that can be configured per-pool: e.g., protect reserved throughput for high-tier tenants, allow low-tier to be deferred. Mediation decisions are stored as policy_decision events to maintain explainability.
4) SLA credit math: credits = integrate_over_throttle_window(tenant_reserved_share * duration * sla_factor * priority_multiplier). Implement a reconciliation guard that prevents applying credits for the same request range twice by keeping a reconciliation cursor per pool.
5) Retrospective adjustments: support adjustment events with idempotency tokens and a backwards-application window (e.g., up to 90 days) after which manual review is required.

Data model and schema notes (implementation-ready):
- event_stream table (write-once append): fields as above; sequence_id used for idempotency.
- micro_ledger table: partitioned by tenant_id + date; columns: window_start_ms, reserved_debit_units, burst_debit_units, applied_sla_credit_units, reconciliation_cursor_id.
- reconciliation_log table: adjustment_id, source_incident, applied_by, timestamp_ms, delta_units, reason.

Edge cases and trade-offs:
- Granularity vs cost: 1s windows increase storage/compute but are necessary to attribute short throttles. We can compact older windows into hourly aggregates after 30 days.
- Negative balances: allow temporary negative micro-ledger balances but maintain a correction flow that applies credits or charges at the end of the billing period to avoid customer surprises.
- Cross-pool events: a request may be retried across pools; attribution will favor the pool that ultimately served the request. If served partial tokens across pools, split attribution by real served tokens.

Testing and verification plan:
- Unit tests for ledger idempotency and sequence handling.
- Synthetic load test: create controlled throttle episodes in a dedicated staging cluster and assert micro-ledger attribution and credit math.
- Fuzz tests for overlapping events and out-of-order event arrival.
- Regression suite to ensure we do not change current bill totals for accounts without throttles.

Observability and UX:
- New console view: "Throttle episodes" per pool with timeline, affected tenants, policy decisions, and computed credit draft.
- API endpoints: GET /pools/{id}/throttle-episodes and GET /tenants/{id}/micro-ledger?date=YYYY-MM-DD
- Dashboards: per-pool rate of throttle events, credit issuance rate, reconciliation backlog.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): implement event_stream and micro_ledger in staging, enable for one internal test pool.
- Phase 2 (pilot): enable on small set of customer-dedicated pools (opt-in), expose console read-only.
- Phase 3 (enforce): enable across all Dedicated pools; start generating draft credits automatically but hold final credit issuance pending billing team sign-off for first month.

Open questions and decisions needed:
- Do we keep 1s granularity or use 500ms for very short spikes? (Engineering prefers 1s for storage balance).
- Priority weighting model: linear multiplier vs tier-protected quotas—PM decision required.
- Reconciliation retention window: 90 days suggested; legal may want longer.

Related docs and references:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Dedicated+Throttle+Accounting+Design (draft)
- Incident runbook draft: drive.google.com/dedicated-throttle-runbook
- Billing spec inspiration: ENG-34102 (windowed-burst-debit model)

acceptance_criteria: Ledger events are write-once and idempotent under replay scenarios
Per-tenant micro-ledgers reflect token-level attribution for throttle windows with <=1s skew
SLA credit computation matches spec and prevents double-application via reconciliation_cursor
Console shows throttle episodes and draft credits for pilot pools
Billing team verifies draft credits for pilot pools and approves automated issuance before full rollout
